title: Offline retry after a timeout creates a duplicate memory
preconditions: A saves a note while the connection is unreliable.
The first request times out after the server may have committed.

actions.note: A sends a note with a stable client id.

expected_behavior: The retry is idempotent for the same client id.
The archive contains exactly one memory.
The retry reports the saved state truthfully.
candidate_failure_modes: The retry creates a second media reservation.
The first success is reported as failed, so A keeps retrying.

observed_code_behavior: Memory create is idempotent per (space_id, client_id) while the row is live.
Update and delete compare the observed updatedAt; a stale write returns 409 without side effects.
Authorship and authorName are computed per viewer, not stored as a snapshot.

hypothetical_user_behavior:
A fictional participant (Theo Bennett) said: "Removing, not redesigning. Three things I'd take out:

1) The storage meter. It renders a number I can't act on, and it disagreed with itself across a refresh, so I opened Settings to check whether it was real. Cost: one detour per session and a small permanent distrust of every other number in the app.

2) Upgrade prompts inside feature gates. The gate already told me I can't proceed. The prompt is a second dialog I have to dismiss — and at large text in split screen it overlaps the field I was mid-way through typing in. Cost: lost keystrokes, which is a draft loss with extra steps.

3) The manage-subscription link that deep-links into a web view. I come back and my form is cleared. If you must keep a route out, keep my state on the way back.

Keep: the plan explanation. It's the only screen that states the limits in words instead of implying them with a disabled button, and it's the only one I've ever read to the end.

What breaks if all three go: nothing functional — a few support tickets asking what the limits are, which the plan explanation already answers.

One thing to fix before removing anything: the paywall reports "network error" when the response is a 402. On a patchy train connection I genuinely cannot tell whether I'm offline or gated, so I retry a payment I've already been charged for. The app should not lie about network state — that's the one line of copy I'd rewrite today."
